s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive umbilical discomfort with a firm, ulcerated nodule and associated abdominal mass
salient_findings: Firm, ulcerated nodule at the umbilicus
Poorly defined, firm mass in the right hypochondrium
key_facts: 55-year-old man with no significant medical history
10-month history of spontaneous, progressively painful umbilical discomfort
Firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender
Umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm and bled on contact
Deep palpation of the abdomen revealed a poorly defined, firm mass approximately 8 cm in diameter in the right hypochondrium
Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth
Irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm
Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion

raw.champion: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a painful umbilical nodule with a biopsy demonstrating well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma, along with irregular thickening of the right third of the transverse colon on CT, suggests a metastatic lesion from a colorectal primary, which is consistent with Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Transverse colon cancer
rejected.why: While the CT shows thickening of the transverse colon, the primary complaint and biopsy were of the umbilical lesion, suggesting metastasis rather than a primary colon cancer.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the cecum
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence pointing to the cecum as the primary site of the adenocarcinoma, and the findings are more suggestive of metastasis to the umbilicus from a colorectal cancer.

rejected.label: Metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma to the umbilicus
rejected.why: The biopsy and imaging findings are more consistent with a colorectal primary than a gastric primary, given the involvement of the transverse colon.

rejected.label: Mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colon
rejected.why: While this could be a subtype of the primary cancer, the information provided does not specifically suggest mucinous adenocarcinoma, and the key finding of an umbilical metastasis (Sister Mary Joseph nodule) is more directly addressed by the chosen champion.
